title: Orchestrated cutover safety lattice and standby health fabric
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Context: Our current region failover relies on coarse liveness probes and a simple priority list. Customers running latency-sensitive workloads have hit outages when a cold standby is promoted because KV cache priming, model variant compatibility (quantized vs fp16), and transient capacity pressure weren’t verified before cutover. This ticket designs and implements a safety lattice + health fabric that composes multiple readiness signals into a single Cutover Readiness Score, and gates automated region/tier routing and fallback model promotions on that score.

Goal: Reduce customer-facing failed cutovers to near zero by ensuring warm-standby readiness before traffic is routed. Provide operator-visible signals and an automated prefill + sanity-check workflow that can be exercised during canary and automated failover.

Scope: Build the Readiness Scoring service (region-router extension), the Prefill/Probe job to warm KV/model caches, bond model-variant compatibility checks, and a Console view for readiness and rollback triggers. Integrate with existing autoscaling and Dedicated capacity APIs. Rollout behind a feature flag with staged region canaries.

Non-goals: Replacing full chaos engineering for cutovers (we will add tests but not a full chaos suite in this ticket). Major autoscaler refactor (only integration points).

Design summary:
- Signals to evaluate: KV cache hit ratio (prefill success), model-variant byte-compat/embedding-consistency check, GPU headroom percentage, tail latency p99, recent error rate (5m), and last-successful-health-check timestamp.
- Each signal is normalized to a 0-100 subscore; scores are combined with configurable weights to produce a Cutover Readiness Score (CRS 0-100). Default weighting is conservative: correctness signals (variant compatibility & errors) have higher weight than performance signals.
- Safety lattice: define three explicit modes based on CRS thresholds: SAFE (>=85) -> automated cutover allowed; CAUTIOUS (65-84) -> manual approval required (with suggested mitigations); BLOCKED (<65) -> deny cutover and surface remediation steps.
- Health fabric: compact readiness document per region/model-variant pair with last-probed timestamp, prefill artifact IDs, and eviction-susceptible cache keys. This lives in the region-router cached store (redis) with TTLs and is writable by the Prefill job.
- Prefill job: snapshot of representative recent requests (from replay buffer) used to warm KV and KV-cache-backed features; it executes in a batch pod with a bounded concurrency window to avoid interfering with production capacity. Prefill exposes metrics (keys primed, time-to-warm, error_count).
- Cutover flow: 1) region-router queries readiness store -> 2) if CRS >= SAFE: proceed with cutover; 3) if CAUTIOUS: open a manual approval task to oncall; 4) if BLOCKED: attempt automated remediation (retry prefill up to N times), otherwise abort and notify.

Telemetry / SLOs:
- New metrics: region_cutover_readiness_score (gauge), prefill_success_rate (counter/ratio), standby_kv_hit_ratio (gauge), cutover_rollback_count (counter), cutover_duration_ms (histogram).
- Alerting: fire if region_cutover_readiness_score < 65 for >5 minutes for a region with active traffic draining.

Security / Compliance: Prefill job only runs with redwood-internal role and does not persist customer PII. All prefill traces are sampled and scrubbed. Require security_review_required for the Readiness API changes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Readiness scoring service implemented and unit-tested.
- Prefill job exists and can be started via Console and CLI.
- Cutover gating enforced by region-router behind a feature flag.
- Console shows readiness per-region and per-model-variant with drilldowns.
- Integration test that simulates a planned failover verifies that traffic is only routed when CRS >= SAFE, and that automated remediation runs for CAUTIOUS cases.
- Playbook added to runbook library with manual approval steps and rollback commands.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Weighting model: Use static defaults (fast) vs. ML-based dynamic weighting (better but adds training/validation and risk). Proposal: start with static, add telemetry to evaluate feature importance, revisit later.
- Prefill dataset: use synthetic golden set vs. recent production replay buffer. Proposal: start with small sampled replay buffer held for N hours.
- Storage for health fabric: redis TTL vs. durable store. Proposal: redis for read/latency; persist a compact event to primary datastore on state transitions for auditability.

Dependencies: ENG-612345 (Dedicated autoscaler read API), ENG-507241 (kv-cache inspector instrumentation), PM-422 (console feature flagging for rollout).
